से लेकर प्रेस कॉन्फ्रेंस तक यही नारा दोहराया गया. लेकिन उत्तराखंड के गदरपुर निर्वाचन क्षेत्र में अंतिम मतदाता सूची की पड़ताल के दौरान हमें कुछ और ही कहानी नजर आई. बताते चलें कि उत्तराखंड के गदरपुर निर्वाचन क्षेत्र में फॉर्म 7 (यानि दूसरों के नाम वोटर सूची से हटाने के लिए आवेदन) और फॉर्म 8 (सुधार के लिए आवेदन) के मामलों में यह इलाका राज्य में दूसरे नंबर पर है. यहां 10 असिस्टेंट इलेक्टोरल रजिस्ट्रेशन ऑफिसर्स (एईआरओ) और इलेक्टोरल रजिस्ट्रेशन ऑफिसर (ईआरओ) ने 18 सितंबर और 28 सितंबर- इन दो तारीखों पर कुल 2,742 आपत्तियां दर्ज कीं. ये दोनों तारीखें 13 अगस्त को 'दावे और आपत्तियां' दर्ज करने की समय-सीमा खत्म होने के एक महीने से भी ज्यादा समय बाद की थीं. दूसरी तारीख तो अंतिम मतदाता सूची जारी होने से महज पांच दिन पहले की थी. गदरपुर में, एसआईआर के दौरान अंतिम मतदाता सूची से 5,505 नाम हटाए गए. इनमें से 2,496 नाम एईआरओ द्वारा दर्ज की गई आपत्तियों के आधार पर हटाए गए, जबकि 240 नाम ईआरओ द्वारा दर्ज की गई आपत्तियों के आधार पर हटाए गए. अन्य लोगों द्वारा दर्ज कराई गई आपत्तियों के बाद 240 नाम और हटा दिए गए, जबकि बाकी 2,529 नामों को बिना किसी आपत्ति के ही हटा दिया गया. गौरतलब है कि 'जन प्रतिनिधित्व अधिनियम, 1950' की धारा 22 के तहत, ईआरओ (निर्वाचक रजिस्ट्रीकरण अधिकारी) किसी नाम को तब भी हटा सकता है, जब उसके खिलाफ 'फॉर्म 7' में कोई आपत्ति दर्ज न की गई हो. ऐसा तब किया जा सकता है जब मतदाता की मृत्यु हो गई हो या वह अब उस निर्वाचन क्षेत्र में न रहता हो या किसी अन्य कारण से अयोग्य हो गया हो. हालांकि, ऐसा करने से पहले मतदाता को अपनी बात रखने का उचित अवसर देना अनिवार्य है. मालूम हो कि दावों और आपत्तियों को दर्ज कराने की अवधि 14 जुलाई से 13 अगस्त, 2026 तक थी. उत्तराखंड के मुख्य निर्वाचन अधिकारी द्वारा प्रकाशित 'फॉर्म 10' के रिकॉर्ड के अनुसार, 13 अगस्त तक 4,785 नामों के खिलाफ आपत्तियां दर्ज की गईं, जबकि 2,828 नामों के खिलाफ आपत्तियां समय-सीमा समाप्त होने के बाद दर्ज की गईं. इनमें से 763 आपत्तियां 18 सितंबर को और 1,979 आपत्तियां 28 सितंबर को ईआरओ और एईआरओ द्वारा दर्ज की गईं. बाकी 83 आपत्तियां अन्य लोगों द्वारा दर्ज की गईं, जिनमें भाजपा नेता चंकित हुरिया द्वारा दर्ज कराई गई 27 आपत्तियां भी शामिल हैं. न्यूज़लॉन्ड्री ने गदरपुर की ईआरओ अमृता शर्मा से दावों और आपत्तियों की समय-सीमा खत्म होने के बाद ईआरओ और एईआरओ द्वारा इतनी बड़ी संख्या में आपत्तियां दर्ज करने को लेकर सवाल किया. जवाब में शर्मा ने कहा, "असल में, हमारे अधिकारियों को यह जानकारी नहीं थी कि जो लोग अनुपस्थित थे, उनके लिए भी 'फॉर्म 7' तैयार करना जरूरी है.

items.title: ‘Only demanding our safety on campus’: SRFTI students’ union vice president on FIR after rustication
items.summary: The Satyajit Ray Film and Television Institute (SRFTI) in Kolkata has filed a case against students’ union vice president Shubham Waydande for allegedly assaulting its vice chancellor. Waydande is one of six students the institute rusticated on October 15. He was rusticated for three semesters, while the other five were rusticated for two semesters each. The campus has remained tense for the past month. It all began on September 27, when students protested an event on campus organised by the Akhil Bharatiya Grahak Panchayat, a body affiliated with the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh. Students and organisers clashed. On October 4, a large crowd from outside gathered at the institute’s gate and shouted slogans. There were also reports of stone-pelting and injured students. SRFTI clarifies that disciplinary action against certain students stems from specific acts of misconduct, including vandalism, defacement, and physical assault—not peaceful protest. The Institute upholds the right to peaceful dissent while ensuring accountability under its rules. #SRFTI #PressRelease #DisciplinaryAction #StudentSafety — Satyajit Ray Film & Television Institute (@srfti_official) October 25, 2026 Students are still protesting, demanding campus security and administrative accountability. The police presence on campus has also drawn questions. Waydande has been booked under Sections 126(2), 115(2), 121(1), 221, 351(2), 352, 324(4), 3(5) and 54 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). Waydande told Newslaundry that he and a few other students were holding a peaceful protest outside the vice chancellor’s office on October 15. The vice chancellor, he said, was already surrounded by security personnel. As far as he knows, someone threw a stone at a window, but he does not know who. The next day, the vice chancellor said the office had been vandalised and announced that CCTV cameras would be installed. Six students were rusticated. According to Waydande, the students asked the vice-chancellor why the administrative gates were closed, why students were not being given access to facilities, and why rusticated students were not being allowed to meet the registrar. items.title: Ajay Devgn moves Bombay High Court against Maharashtra FDA notice over Vimal Elaichi ad
items.summary: Bollywood actor Ajay Devgn has approached the Bombay High Court challenging a show-cause notice issued by the Maharashtra Food and Drugs Administration (FDA) over his appearance in advertisements for ‘Vimal Elaichi' [Ajay Devgan v. State of Maharashtra & Ors.]. The petition is likely to be heard by a division bench of Chief Justice Mahesh C Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna on November 4. Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna The dispute stems from regulatory notices issued by the Maharashtra FDA alleging that advertisements for ‘Vimal Elaichi’ amount to the surrogate promotion of ‘Vimal Pan Masala’, a chewable product banned within Maharashtra. Similar notices were also served to co-brand ambassadors Shah Rukh Khan and Tiger Shroff. In his petition, Devgn has challenged the constitutionality of the provisions of the FDA regulations. He has argued that the notice was arbitrarily served directly on him as an actor rather than on the manufacturing company. Previously, the product's manufacturer, PB Agro, approached the Delhi High Court in August to quash the notices. However, the High Court dismissed the plea , ruling that it lacked territorial jurisdiction. The Court observed that since the controversy concerned actions taken by the Mumbai FDA regarding alleged activities in Maharashtra, the State’s courts were the appropriate forum. After this dismissal, Devgn has now moved the Bombay High Court. Devgn is being represented by DSK legal team led by partners Parag Kandhar and Chandrima Das.

items.title: Choosing your counsel in the Supreme Court: Why strategy matters more than a big name
items.summary: In litigation, we often hear "facts win cases." After years of managing litigation, I have realised that in the Supreme Court, facts alone do not win cases; strategy does. And the most critical part of that strategy is choosing the right arguing counsel. I want to share a recent experience that taught me this lesson the hard way. Journey of a case We lost at every stage. The statutory appeal was dismissed. The statutory revision failed. The writ petition was not entertained. With little hope left, we filed a letters patent appeal (LPA) before the Division Bench. This time, we engaged a non-senior counsel who had actually read our brief threadbare. She knew the record. She persuaded the Division Bench not by rhetoric, but by methodical presentation. We won. The Division Bench reversed all the earlier findings. That victory brought us to the Supreme Court - the last forum for justice - as the opposite side challenged the Division Bench order. Where we lost the plot For the Supreme Court, the management decided to go with a very big name - a top-billed Senior Counsel whose name alone, we thought, would carry weight. It was a conscious choice of brand over fit. And that is where we lost. On the day of hearing, the Bench was asking pointed questions. They wanted spontaneous answers from the record. They wanted to be persuaded on a very narrow legal point that had convinced the Division Bench. Instead, the arguing counsel was not fully familiar with the factual nuances, sought adjournments and could not gauge the pulse of the Bench. The Judges' minds were made up in the first 10 minutes and we could not chase their opinion or course-correct. The special leave petition (SLP) was allowed against us. Years of hard work, culminating in a hard-fought LPA victory, was undone in a 15-minute hearing. The lesson for young lawyers and in-house counsel As young lawyers and in-house counsel, we are often under tremendous pressure from management to engage the "biggest" name when a matter reaches the Supreme Court. We think, "It is the Supreme Court, we must take the biggest shot." This is a flawed approach. The Supreme Court is not a place for posturing. It is a court of persuasion. 1. items.title: Kerala High Court rejects Kudale Committee's report on Vizhinjham port coastal erosion; orders fresh panel
items.summary: In a verdict of significant importance to coastal environmental concerns, the Kerala High Court on Friday set aside the study report of an expert committee headed by MD Kudale on the coastal erosion allegedly caused by the construction of Vizhinjam International Seaport [Nirmala Johny & ors v State of Kerala & ors]. Justice Harisankar V Menon held that the committee's constitution was flawed due to concerns over conflicts of interest involving its members and directed that its final report should not be acted upon. "This Court is of the opinion that the challenge against the constitution of the Committee pursuant to Ext.P11 Government Order and the opinion of the Committee, raised by the petitioners is only to be accepted," the Court stated. It particularly noted that Kudale had earlier served as an expert member of the technical sub-committee which was involved in developing the Vizhinjam Port project. " If, as a matter of fact, he was so engaged, this Court is of the opinion that inclusion of Sri.Kudale in the Committee constituted pursuant to Ext.P11 Government Order ought to have been avoided. As already noticed, the earlier involvement of Sri Kudale is not disputed by any of the respondents, " the Court said. Hence, it directed the State government to constitute a fresh independent expert committee to study the alleged coastal erosion due to the establishment of the deep water port. Justice Harisankar V Menon The judgment came on a petition filed by 128 residents of fishing villages situated within 20 km north of Vizhinjam, who claimed that construction of the port had caused severe coastal erosion, resulting in the loss of their homes. They challenged the expert committee constituted by the Kerala government in October 2022 to examine whether port construction had contributed to coastal erosion and whether measures can be taken to address it. The four-member committee was headed by MD Kudale, Former Additional Director, Central Water and Power Research Station (CWPRS), Pune. Its other members were Dr Riji John, Dr Tejal Kanitkar and Dr PK Chandramohan. The petitioners argued that the committee lacked independence because some members had professional associations with the port project or the companies connected to it. items.title: Collegium recommends appointment of 5 judicial officers as Madhya Pradesh High Court judges
items.summary: The Supreme Court Collegium on Friday recommended the appointment of five judicial officers as judges of the Madhya Pradesh High Court. The judicial officers recommended for elevation are: - Renuka Kanchan; - Krishnamurty Mishra; - Virendra Singh Rajput; - Mamta Jain; - Ashita Shrivastava. The Collegium had also recommended the appointment of seven advocates as judges of the High Court on October 26. The Collegium's recommendations will now be forwarded to the Central government for further processing. The appointments will take effect once the Central government clears the recommendations and the President of India issues the necessary warrants of appointment. The Madhya Pradesh High Court has a sanctioned strength of 53 judges. As of September 2026, the High Court had 38 serving judges against a sanctioned strength of 53, leaving 15 vacancies. items.title: Amid protests, Allahabad High Court tells young lawyers to focus on career, not social media likes
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court on Friday observed that young lawyers should focus on building their careers rather than generating likes on social media [Rajesh v State of UP] Justice Arun Kumar Singh Deshwal made the observation while commenting on certain media posts of lawyers regarding the functioning of the High Court. The Court said incomplete and twisted information may lead to unnecessary differences between the bar and the bench. "Young advocates should concentrate on their studies as well as on preparing their cases to build their careers instead of concentrating on increasing their social media likes. Young advocates are the future of the High Court. Most of the Judges as well as senior advocates of this Court are trying their best to create a good atmosphere for the future of young lawyers, who in future will become senior advocates as well as Judges of this High Court," the Court said. Justice Arun Kumar Singh Deshwal The Court made the comments in the context of advocates' ongoing protest against alleged ill-treatment of a lawyer by Justice Ajay Bhanot earlier this week. The issue stemmed from an incident in Justice Bhanot's court when he made a lawyer apologise to a Superintendent of Police (SP) for objecting to the officer sitting in a seat usually reserved for lawyers. The lawyer had asked the SP to move further back. The bar association said that a separate chair was being placed in Justice Bhanot's courtroom for police officers and other high-ranking officials. The bar body alleged that the judge threatened to jail the lawyer and also ridiculed another senior counsel. In a statement released on Tuesday, the association warned that its members would boycott Justice Bhanot's court if no action is taken. Though there was no formal call for boycotting the judge, lawyers on Wednesday vandalised his courtroom . Justice Deshwal, whose courtroom is near Justice Bhanot's courtroom, has been unable to hear cases since Wednesday due to the protest by lawyers. items.title: Kerala HC orders dignified burial of Indian whose body remained in UAE for 18 months amid family dispute
items.summary: The Kerala High Court recently stepped in to ensure the dignified burial of a 71-year-old Indian man who died in March 2025 in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and whose body remained there due to a dispute between his relatives as to where he should be buried [ Mary Victoria v Ministry of External Affairs & ors ]. Justice PV Kunhikrishnan passed the order after observing that disputed between the deceased man's relatives as to whether he should be buried in India at the family tomb or abroad cannot indefinitely prolong his burial. The Court further emphasised that every person deserves a dignified burial regardless of their financial or social status. Ensuring a decent burial is the responsibility of relatives, society, and ultimately the State, if the others fail to fulfil that duty, the Court said. " It is the duty of each and every one of us to see that the dead body of a person is buried decently, whether he is a poor man or a wealthy man. There is no ‘poor man's dead body’ or ‘wealthy man’s dead body’. Let us not call it like that. Death has erased those distinctions. The mortal remains of all human beings are similar. A dead body deserves no label, but it deserves respect and dignity. This is part of the right under Article 21 of the Constitution of India, " the Court added in its October 28 ruling. Justice PV Kunhikrishnan Kerala High Court It is the duty of each and every one of us to see that the dead body of a person is buried decently, whether poor or wealthy... A dead body deserves no label, but it deserves respect and dignity. Robert Francis Sahayan, a 71-year-old Indian citizen, died by suicide in the UAE on March 26, 2025 and since then, his mortal remains had been kept at the forensic laboratory of a hospital in Ajman. items.title: Holy cow, unholy sentence
items.summary: In a secular constitutional republic, criminal courts are tasked with measuring guilt against the penal code, weighing evidence under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam and sentencing offenders within the rational bounds of statutory discretion. On October 26, an additional sessions court at Kalol in Gandhinagar district of Gujarat chose a rather different source of jurisprudence. Judge Brijeshkumari Rameshwarsinh Rajput sentenced three men - Wasim, Mohammed Rafiq and Ashfaq - to rigorous imprisonment for life based on the recovery of 277 kilograms of beef, seized during a raid on a village house in Jamla. To justify locking three men in prison until their natural death, the court found standard principles of proportionality, penology, or individual reformation as petty distractions - far too mundane for the case in hand. Instead, the judgment embarked on an expansive theological excursion. Drawing directly from the Rigveda , the Manusmriti and the Harivamsa Purana , the court noted that the cow houses 33 crore deities; that the sun and moon dwell within its eyes; that Brahma, Vishnu and Mahesh inhabit its horns; and that the four legs of the bovine represent the four Vedas. Then came the judicial diagnosis: if those who slaughter cows are not handed life sentences, “Gau Mata will become extinct from the earth.” It is an extraordinary proposition. One is left to wonder whether the judge was presiding over a criminal sessions court or sitting as an ecclesiastical tribunal enforcing a theological code. Extinction as a sentencing policy Consider the zoological panic at the heart of the order. The judgment warns that failure to impose the maximum punishment will cause cows to vanish from the face of the earth. The Dodo succumbed to sailors. The Woolly Mammoth fell to climate shifts. The Indian bovine, boasting a head count of over 300 million head of cattle , was apparently three slaughterhouse knives away from joining them. Yes, India possesses the largest bovine population on the planet, with over 300 million head of cattle. The risk facing Indian cattle on the streets of Gandhinagar is rarely premature extinction. It is the ingestion of municipal single-use plastic, starvation in decrepit, State-funded gaushalas and road accidents caused by administrative abandonment. The contradiction borders on farce. items.title: Delhi court orders Sukesh Chandrashekhar's release in 2017 PC Act case
items.summary: A Delhi court has ordered alleged conman Sukesh Chandrashekhar’s release in a 2017 corruption case. Special Judge (PC Act) Vidya Prakash of the Rouse Avenue Court passed an order on October 28, holding that Chandrashekhar has already been in jail for a period longer than the maximum punishment for the offences he faces. “Consequently, it is hereby directed that the applicant/accused namely Sukesh @ Sukash Chandrashekhar be not detained during pendency of trial in this case, and he be released from jail forthwith, if not required in any other case,” the Court ordered. Chandrashekhar was arrested on October 24, 2017, in this case. The FIR was registered by the Delhi Police Crime Branch. According to records, he spent eight years, nine months and 14 days in custody, even after excluding periods of parole and interim bail. He is charged with the offences under Section 12 of the Prevention of Corruption Act and Section 120B IPC, which carry a maximum sentence of seven years. The prosecution opposed the plea, citing 29 criminal cases against him across several states, some under MCOCA, and an apprehension that he could influence witnesses. It was also argued that he had not furnished sureties after being granted bail under Section 436A on September 21, 2022, and should not benefit from his own wrong. However, the Court held that the second proviso to Section 436A of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) is mandatory. As per the same, no person shall in any case be detained during the period of investigation inquiry or trial for more than the maximum period of imprisonment provided for the said offence under that law. It found the prosecution had not shown that the accused caused any delay in proceedings. Therefore, the Court ordered his release in the case. [Read Order]

They further submitted that they were neither the owners nor the creators or administrators of the YouTube channel 'Karnataka Honey Trap', which they claimed was created and operated by someone else. The Court noted that a co-accused facing similar allegations had already secured interim anticipatory bail. It further observed that granting interim protection subject to stringent conditions would not hamper the investigation. “Otherwise, the personal liberty of the petitioner guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitution would be frustrated” the court observed. The Court directed each petitioner to execute a personal bond of ₹1 lakh with one surety for the like sum in the event of arrest. On October 23, Bengaluru-based television channel Power TV's Managing Director Rakesh Shetty secured interim anticipatory bail in the same case. items.title: Does Punjab government have ₹520? P&H High Court calls out State's delaying tactics in DA case
items.summary: The Punjab and Haryana High Court on Friday said Punjab government's conduct regarding the payment of Dearness Allowance (DA) to employees and pensioners did not inspire confidence, as it had failed to take steps to get its appeal against the High Court's ruling listed before the Supreme Court. On August 3, the High Court had directed the State to release all up-to-date pending installments of dearness allowance/dearness relief (DA/DR) to all its employees and pensioners respectively at the same rates as paid to the All India Services (IAS/IPS/IFS) officers serving within Punjab. The judgment, which also bars the government from resorting to any unproductive expenditures such as large-scale advertising campaigns in print or social media till non-payment of the dues, has been challenged by the State before the Supreme Court. However, the petition has been before the top court's registry since September 1 owing to defects. While hearing a plea alleging non-compliance with the direction for filing of compliance affidavit by Chief Secretary KAP Sinha, a bench of Justice Vinod S Bhardwaj and Justice Ravinder Malik today said there appeared to be a deliberate attempt to interfere in the administration of justice. "When you go through the sequence of events, there is hardly a valid reason for non-listing of the SLP. It seems a deliberate designed effort to ensure that the SLP is not listed at all, considering the fact that you have been successful in getting other SLPs listed before Supreme Court at a short notice of 24 hours," the bench said. items.title: Lawyers submitting fake affidavits spoil the faith of Bar-friendly judges: Kerala High Court
items.summary: Kerala High Court judge Justice Kauser Edappagath on Friday revealed in open court that there have been several instances of advocates filing fake affidavits. The day of hearings was drawing to a close when the judge, who was hearing bail matters all day, was confronted with a case where the counsel representing the accused sought relief on the ground that a settlement had been reached with the complainant. Justice Edappagath said that he cannot accept such submissions or affidavits on blind faith without giving the prosecution time to get instructions and verify its authenticity. " There have been so many cases where affidavits are filed and when later the prosecutor is asked to get instructions, it turns out they are fake. Just ask the prosecutor ," Justice Edappagath orally remarked. The judge also questioned why lawyers seem to work under the impression that the court can grant bail or any other relief on a plea moved mere hours earlier, without giving a chance for the State prosecutor to get instructions on the matter. " I will not accept any settlement until the prosecutor gets instructions. That is not going to happen. You file a petition at 1 PM and expect to get an order granting bail by 4 PM? They have to get instructions ," he said. As the final bell of the day rang at 4:00 PM, Justice Edappagath rose and rather dejectedly added, " We are all working day and night, but still you (lawyers) are concerned about your one case only. You people will spoil a bar-friendly judge. "

items.title: Bombay High Court slams former Chief Justice's special officer for misusing his name in trust appointments matter
items.summary: The Bombay High Court has quashed an administrative directive issued by the former Chief Justice's special officer that had halted the appointment of trustees to Shree Saptashrung Nivasini Devi Trust in Nashik [Vishnu Trimbak Warungase & Ors v. State of Maharashtra & Ors] . A Division Bench of Justices GS Kulkarni and Neela Gokhale held that the officer, Anju Shende, acted with ‘gross impropriety’, without lawful authority and misused the name of the Chief Justice. Justices GS Kulkarni and Neela Gokhale The controversy arose after Shende sent an email to the Nashik Principal District and Sessions Judge on March 14, 2026, ordering the immediate withdrawal of a recommended list of five trustees finalised on March 12 following an interview process. The participants in the selection process for trustee appointment approached the court challenging the communication. items.title: Law student moves Kerala High Court against restrictions under new internship policy
items.summary: A law student awaiting enrolment after completing his LL.B course has approached the Kerala High Court challenging the restrictions under the High Court's revised internship policy [Austin Sunny v High Court of Kerala & ors]. The High Court heard the plea on Wednesday and directed its authorities to issue a temporary entry pass to the student, one Austin Suney, who was denied permission to attend court proceedings as an intern. As per the revised internship policy , only students who are in the last two years of their law courses would be allowed to undertake internships at the High Court. This restriction raised concerns over whether students who had completed their courses and were awaiting examination results or enrolment as advocates could continue interning with individual practising lawyers and attend court proceedings. Justice PV Kunhikrishnan granted interim relief to the petitioner, directing authorities to issue a temporary entry pass to him subject to compliance with the internship policy and a written assurance from the advocate confirming that the student is interning under him. The Court, however, observed that the question of whether the internship policy applies to students who do not meet its eligibility criteria could be decided later. " After hearing both sides, I think an interim order can be passed as far as the petitioner alone is concerned. The larger issue can be decided later, " the Court added. It also directed the petitioner to add the High Court Advocates' Association as an additional respondent and asked the respondents to file counter affidavits. Justice PV Kunhikrishnan Suney, a student of Bharat Mata School of Legal Studies at Aluva, completed his final semester examinations on September 16, 2026 and is currently awaiting his results. He joined law firm Ninan & Mathew Advocates for an internship; however, when he approached the High Court authorities for an entry pass for attending court proceedings, he was informed that only students currently studying in the final year were eligible. Despite producing a certificate from his college confirming his student status, he was denied the entry pass without any written reasons. items.title: High Court can order restoration of electricity in disputes involving power theft: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday held that High Courts can order the restoration of electricity supply that was disconnected over disputed allegations of theft, but advised against adopting a liberal approach in such cases [ Dakshin Gujarat Vij Vs Vaibhav Crusher ]. A Bench of Justices Manoj Misra and KV Viswanathan observed that electricity is essential for life and livelihood, and that its deprivation could have serious consequences. Therefore, constitutional courts can intervene to protect consumers against arbitrary disruption of electricity supply by electricity distribution companies, it held. " Electricity is an essential commodity necessary for both life and livelihood. Its deprivation may have serious consequences. In an appropriate case, the High Court may be justified in exercising its constitutional powers to protect a person from an arbitrary action of the State and its instrumentalities including a distribution licensee, " the judgment stated. The Court, however, cautioned that a liberal approach may not be appropriate in cases involving allegations of electricity theft. It said that in such cases - involving allegations of theft that are yet to be finally decided - courts should impose appropriate conditions before ordering the reconnection of electricity. "In cases of theft, which necessarily involves a criminal intent (i.e. mens rea), adoption of a liberal approach may not be appropriate. Rather, each case should be addressed on its own facts and if the facts so warrant, the High Court might be justified in even declining the prayer for restoration of electricity supply till entire amount, provisionally assessed, is deposited. In short, a circumspect approach is required while dealing with petitions seeking restoration of supply of electricity disconnected on ground of theft," the October 26 ruling stated. Justice Manoj Misra and Justice KV Viswanathan The judgment was delivered in appeals filed by Dakshin Gujarat Vij Company Limited and Paschim Gujarat Vij Company Limited against orders passed by the Gujarat High Court. One of the disputes concerned Vaibhav Metal Crusher, which had received a supplementary electricity bill demanding approximately ₹93 lakh towards alleged electricity theft, besides ₹23.45 lakh as compounding charges. items.title: Dual PAN card case: Allahabad High Court grants bail to Azam Khan, refuses stay on conviction

Justice Samit Gopal suspended their sentences while their revision petitions challenging their conviction are pending. The Court observed that Khan and his son had already served substantial portions of their fixed-term sentences. "Looking to the nature of occurrence, period of detention of the accused/revisionists, the fact that the case in hand is for a fixed term of sentence, the present case is a fit case where the accused/revisionists... be enlarged on bail," the Court said. Justice Samit Gopal The case stems from a 2019 complaint by BJP leader Akash Saxena alleging that Abdullah Azam Khan in a planned conspiracy with his father procured a second PAN card with a forged date of birth to bypass age criteria to fraudulently contest the 2017 Uttar Pradesh Assembly polls from Rampur's Suar constituency. Appearing for the convicts, Senior Advocates Abhishek Manu Singhvi and N I Jafri , assisted by Advocate Shashwat Anand, submitted that while Azam Khan had undergone over four years and one month in custody, Abdullah Azam had served over three years and six months. Opposing the plea, Additional Advocate General Anoop Trivedi and counsel for the informant argued that the convicts actively forged statutory documents to manipulate elections. Admitting the criminal revisions, the High Court expedited the matter and listed it for final hearing in the third week of January 2027. While the Court granted bail to Khan and his son, it refused to stay their conviction. The denial of relief means they remain disqualified from contesting elections in view of the provisions of the Representation of the People Act, 1951. items.title: Madras High Court compares appointment of Srirangam pontiff to election of Pope, sets deadline to fill position
items.summary: The Madras High Court recently drew parallels between the election of the Pope and the appointment of the Srirangam temple's pontiff while ordering that the post which has remained vacant since 2018 be filled within six months [Veera Raghavan Vs State of TN] A division bench of Justices GR Swaminathan and P Murugan observed that those responsible for selecting the pontiff should remain inside the Mutt until a successor is chosen. " Just as the Cardinals are locked inside the Sistine Chapel and the doors are opened only when the white smoke emanates from the chimney indicating the selection of the Pope, the Sthalattars should be locked inside the Mutt premises and allowed to come out only after resolving the issue," said the Court. Justice GR Swaminathan, Justice P Murugan The Court was hearing a public interest litigation (PIL) petition filed by S Veeraraghavan, a devotee belonging to the Sri Vaishnava Tenkalai sect, seeking the appointment of a successor to the Sriranganarayana Jeeyar. The bench noted that the Jeeyars' lineage dates to the 12th century. Sri Ramanujacharya had devised an elaborate system for administering the Srirangam Ranganathaswamy Temple, with the Jeeyar occupying an apex position. Apart from performing spiritual functions, the Jeeyar exercises administrative responsibilities and acts as a neutral arbiter to ensure compliance with the Agamas. The 50th Jeeyar, who assumed office in 1989, died in 2018 without nominating a successor. Under the Mutt's customs, the successor must be selected by the Sthalattars, either unanimously or by majority. However, the Court observed that the prolonged vacancy benefited the Sthalattars and Bhattars, among whom the Jeeyar's powers had been distributed. " Since there is no Jeeyar, there is no one to question them also. There is no incentive for them to choose the next Jeeyar. On the other hand, the status quo suits them. But it certainly infringes the rights of the devotees. " The Court held that the failure to appoint a successor violates the fundamental rights of the Mutt's disciples under Article 25 of the Constitution. It noted that the Tamil Nadu Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) Department had invited applications in 2021 and received responses from qualified candidates but had taken no consequential steps. It expressed shock that the previous Jeeyar had purportedly been appointed through proceedings issued by a temple official under Section 55(1) of the Tamil Nadu HR&CE Act, 1959.

items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday struck down Karnataka Civil Services (Validation of Selection and Appointment of 2011 Batch Gazetted Probationers) Act, 2022, which validated around 191 appointments that had earlier been cancelled over allegations of corruption and nepotism [Srinavasa T v State of Karnataka and Others] A Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran held that the 2022 law was unconstitutional, as the State legislature could not overturn the cancellation of these appointments after the decision had been upheld by constitutional courts. The PIL was cursorily dealt with, and the later Writ Petition was also dealt with in a similar manner, throwing to winds every tenet of law; upholding an enactment clearly beyond the scope of the powers conferred on the law-making authority and bordering on the absurd,” the bench said. items.title: Kerala High Court upholds relief to Wipro over 'Brahmins' sambar powder trademark
items.summary: The Kerala High Court recently upheld the temporary injunction imposed on Greenmount Spices, restricting it from using the ‘Brahmins’ or ‘Brahmins Sambar Powder’ trademarks until a trademark infringement suit filed by Wipro Enterprises is decided. [ Greenmount Spices Private Limited v. Wipro Enterprises Private Limited ] Justice CS Dias opined that Wipro had established a prima facie case to support its claim of prior commercial use of the trademarks in question. " I am satisfied that the respondent has established a prima facie case, supported by materials indicating prior commercial use of the ‘Brahmins’ trade mark. The balance of convenience is also in favour of the respondent. If the impugned use is ultimately found to infringe the respondent’s [Wipro] rights, its continued use may erode the distinctiveness of the trade mark and cause injury not readily compensable in damages. These conclusions are tentative and shall not prejudice the final adjudication of the suit, " the Court said in its judgment. Justice CS Dias In 2024, Wipro instituted a suit before a district court to restrain Greenmount from manufacturing, advertising, selling or exporting food products, including sambar powder, and from using Wipro's trademarks, or any identical or deceptively similar marks, including ‘Brahmins’ or ‘Brahmins Sambar Powder’, on packaging, websites or as a trade name or domain name. Along with the suit, Wipro filed an application for a temporary injunction against Greenmount. The district court allowed Wipro's application and temporarily injuncted Greenmount from using ‘Brahmins’ or ‘Brahmins Sambar Powder’ trademarks. Greenmount subsequently moved the High Court challenging the district court's temporary injunction. They claimed that their trademark is ‘Greenmount’, whereas ‘Brahmin Sambar Powder’ is used only descriptively to identify the product, not as a trademark. They argued that the word ‘Brahmin’ denotes a traditional Hindu community and and sambar is an integral part of their cuisine. This makes the expression ‘Brahmin Sambar Powder’ a generic and descriptive one that is protected by Section 30(2)(a) of the Trade Marks Act, 1999. Wipro opposed Greenmount's appeal pointing out that it acquired the Brahmins group business together with its trade mark and goodwill and is now the owner of the trade mark ‘Brahmins’. items.title: Supreme Court reserves verdict on ED's Article 32 plea for CBI probe against Mamata Banerjee
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday reserved its verdict on a petition filed by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) seeking a probe by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) into alleged obstructions during its search operations at the Kolkata premises of political consultancy firm I-PAC [ ED v. State of West Bengal & Ors. ]. The matter concerns an incident from January 8, when TMC leader and the then West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee, entered the premises of political consultancy firm Indian Pac Consulting Private Limited (I-PAC) and allegedly took away certain sensitive files. A Bench of Justices PK Mishra and NV Anjaria reserved orders after hearing arguments on behalf Banerjee, the ED, and other respondents. "Arguments concluded, reserved for order/judgment," the Court said. Justice PK Mishra and Justice NV Anjaria The ED had moved the top court under Article 32 of the Constitution, alleging that on January 8, Banerjee and senior State police officials barged into I-PAC's Kolkata office and the residence of its co-founder Pratik Jain while searches were underway in connection with a 2020 coal smuggling money laundering case against businessman Anup Majee. The agency claimed that the intervention resulted in the forced removal of critical physical and electronic evidence. items.title: Supreme Court to vet RBI’s digital fraud regulations before notification, says banks must compensate victims
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday said that it would examine the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI’s) proposed anti-cyber fraud regulations before they are notified. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was hearing suo motu proceedings concerning digital arrest scams. The case arose from a senior citizen couple’s complaint of losing ₹1.05 crore to impersonators using forged judicial orders. It said that the regulations must require financial institutions to compensate victims where fraud results from failed due diligence. Compensation must be at least equivalent to the customer’s loss, the Court said. “The amount will remain intact. The bank will have to pay. That is the only way,” the CJI remarked, stressing that liability could not stop with individual officers. Justice Joymalya Bagchi, CJI Surya Kant and Justice V Mohana Justice Bagchi questioned why financial institutions should not face strict liability when their failure to provide safeguards enables misuse of banking products. Banks must become a “protective umbrella” for customers, the CJI said, asking why an unusually large transfer from a pensioner’s savings should not trigger intervention. The Court emphasised mandatory suspension of unusual transactions, automated reporting and physical verification of genuineness. “ Do they have sufficient teeth to control it?” the CJI asked about RBI’s regulations. “Unless there is a penal direction to these banks, they will never mend their ways.” He questioned the RBI’s “soft-pedalling” through consultations with banks when action was sought against them and contrasted banks’ loan settlements with their accountability towards victims. Justice Bagchi sought data on suspicious transactions blocked and those unreported before fraud subsequently emerged. Appearing for the RBI, Attorney General for India R Venkataramani said that bank employees had also prevented fraud and complaints had fallen by about 50%. He sought time for technical integration, proposing notification by November 30 and operationalisation by December 31. The Bench sought the draft regulations and a list of authorised financial institutions. “The regulation must include a liability clause. Otherwise, we will enforce it through a judicial order,” the CJI said. items.title: Bombay High Court restrains ex-Clippings CEO Vinayak Shrivastav from alienating assets over ₹222 crore suit
items.summary: The Bombay High Court has restrained Vinayak Shrivastav, the former Chief Executive Officer of US-based Clippings LLC, from selling, transferring or creating third-party rights over his personal assets. [Clippings LLC & Ors. v. Vinayak Shrivastav & Ors.] This directive came in a commercial suit filed by court-appointed caretakers (receivers) of Clippings, seeking to recover approximately ₹222.62 crore (around $23.27 million) allegedly siphoned off by Shrivastav and routed to his family members and affiliate entities. Justice Arif Doctor held that the company had established a strong preliminary case of fraud. The bench observed that refusing interim protection at this stage would be counterproductive. "In my view, at this stage to deny the Plaintiffs the limited ad interim relief sought on the basis of the defences which have been raised would be to miss the wood for the trees and to ignore the elephant in the room," the Court said. Justice Arif Doctor The allegation against Shrivastav is that he procured a $53.15 million loan from Park View SPV III in October 2025 using forged documents, including fabricated signatures and false bank records. The company alleged that instead of using the loan to refinance earlier corporate debt owed to an investor named Bluestone, Shrivastav diverted tens of millions of dollars to himself, his family and related corporate entities. The defendants argued that the lawsuit should be dismissed because the court-appointed receivers had suppressed material agreements and corporate emails. Justice Doctor dismissed this defence, emphasising that Shrivastav had not confronted the core allegations. "Defendant No. 1 has made no attempt in the Affidavit in Reply or in the oral contention to meet the most serious allegations of forgery and fabrication concerning the Credit Agreement," the judge said. The Court noted that the plaintiffs were independent court officers acting without personal interest to safeguard the company. "The very manner in which the Defendants have resisted making the disclosures only amplifies the need for the same," the judge said. Under the directions, all defendants must submit sworn affidavits within ten days detailing their worldwide assets, bank accounts and six years of tax filings. items.title: Kerala judge whose son caused fatal accident moves High Court seeking anticipatory bail
items.summary: The Additional District Judge whose his son was recently involved in a car crash that killed a scooter rider, has moved the Kerala High Court seeking anticipatory bail. The petition is listed for hearing today before Justice Kauser Edappagath . The accused-judge's 17-year-old son was driving a Mercedes-Benz car when he hit a two-wheeler in Kochi's Cheranalloor on October 25, killing the scooter rider, one Jayabalakrishnan. The judge who is posted at a Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (MACT) at Iranjalakuda in Thrissur district, has been arraigned as an accused in the FIR registered by the Police after the crash. The FIR includes offences punishable under Section 105 (culpable homicide not amounting to murder) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS) read with Sections 181, 183, 199A(1), and 199A(2) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (MVA). Section 199A provides that when a minor commits a motor vehicle offence, the guardian or vehicle owner is presumed to be responsible and can be prosecuted and punished, subject to statutory exceptions. In his plea before the Kerala High Court seeking anticipatory bail, the judge has claimed that he had no knowledge whatsoever that the vehicle had been removed from the premises. He learnt of it only when he was awakened by a telephone call informing him that his minor son had taken the vehicle out when he was asleep and gotten into the accident. He has also pointed out that Section 105 BNS requires explicit mens rea—specifically, the knowledge that the act is likely to cause death. " Attributing knowledge under Section 105 BNS vicariously to a parent who was sleeping at home when a minor took a vehicle surreptitiously is legally untenable and fundamentally opposed to settled principles of criminal law ", the plea reads. The accused-judge will be represented by advocate John S Ralph. Earlier, the Juvenile Justice Board in Ernakulam had granted bail to the minor on October 26. The State's plea seeking cancellation of the bail is pending before a sessions court. Meanwhile, the family of the man who died in the crash submitted a complaint before the Kerala High Court Chief Justice seeking an enquiry into the judicial officer's conduct. The complaint submitted by the victim's children requested the Chief Justice to examine whether an administrative or disciplinary enquiry is warranted against the judicial officer. items.title: From appetite to austerity: Health underwriting under the DPDP regime

The Act's implementation in the health insurance sector exposes a striking structural tension. The industry’s core model, which relies on exhaustive disclosures at various stages, now has to be reconciled with a legal framework that demands a much narrower, purpose-specific approach to data. At the heart of this conflict lie two cardinal principles of data protection: data minimisation and purpose limitation. For an industry where more data traditionally equals fair risk pricing and coverage sustainability, the DPDP Act’s imposition of data minimization and purpose limitation demands a radical contraction of data appetites. Data minimisation demands a forward-looking assessment: what categories of data are strictly necessary to achieve the articulated purpose? Purpose limitation, in turn, requires clarity at the point of collection about why the data is being gathered and imposes a prohibition on function creep or the gradual expansion of data use beyond its original justification. These principles are reinforced by the requirement that consent be informed, specific, and unambiguous, and that processing beyond the stated purpose is impermissible unless justified by law. items.title: Obligations under CERT-In and DPDP – Not a zero-sum game
items.summary: India is on the brink of a pivotal moment in its data privacy landscape - one that will reshape not only regulatory practice but also the everyday interaction of individuals and businesses with digital ecosystems. With the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (‘DPDP Act’) and its accompanying Rules (‘DPDP Rules’) poised for implementation, the task of integrating this new framework within the existing regulatory regime assumes critical importance. The central issue is whether the DPDP regime will operate in harmony with parallel obligations or whether it risks creating conflicting compliance tracks. The DPDP Act has largely sought to avoid potential conflicts with the erstwhile regulatory framework governing data privacy through the repeal of relevant provisions and rules of the Information Technology Act. A significant exception, however, is the 2022 directions issued by the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (‘CERT-In’) under Section 70-B(6) of the Information Technology Act, 2000 (‘CERT-In Directions’), which continue to survive. In other words, the Act regulates the processing of personal data irrespective of the nature or identity of the entity engaged in such processing. Section 3 of the Act, which sets out the scope of application, makes it evident that the sweep of the DPDP Act is expansive. items.title: Christophe Jaffrelot on CJP, RSS, BJP and the future of Indian democracy | South Central 99
items.summary: In this week’s South Central, hosts Dhanya Rajendran and Pooja Prasanna are joined by political scientist and scholar Professor Christophe Jaffrelot for an extended conversation on the RSS, the BJP, the rise of Hindutva and the changing nature of Indian democracy. Listen and follow on YouTube Listen and follow on Apple Listen and follow on Spotify Dhanya begins by asking Jaffrelot about the student-led protests against the government, which have shifted from demands for better governance and education to concerns over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and the alleged exclusion of millions of voters. Jaffrelot describes this as a transition “from policies to politics”, arguing that the convergence of student movements and opposition parties could be significant. However, he says a larger social movement would need to bring together farmers, workers and Dalit groups, drawing parallels with the JP movement. The conversation then examines the weakening of democratic institutions under the BJP government. Jaffrelot argues that the institutional changes initiated in Gujarat under Narendra Modi were replicated at the national level, pointing to the functioning of the police and judiciary, the diminishing role of parliamentary committees and concerns surrounding the Election Commission. The discussion moves to the relationship between the RSS and Modi. Jaffrelot says Modi has established himself as a national populist leader with a direct relationship with voters, often bypassing the BJP’s traditional organisational structures and the RSS. While the RSS has benefited from the government’s policies and continued to expand its grassroots presence, he warns that it also risks being held accountable for the government’s failures. Jaffrelot also argues that defeating the BJP electorally would not necessarily mean that Hindutva has lost its influence in society. He points to the normalisation of anti-Muslim sentiment and rising hostility towards minorities, saying that reversing these changes would require a broader social movement that goes beyond electoral victories. The conversation then turns to caste politics and the RSS’s attempts to bring different caste groups under the umbrella of Hindutva. Jaffrelot argues that caste-based inequalities remain entrenched, despite efforts to build a broader Hindu identity. items.title: At COP17, the fight is to give women more than a seat at the biodiversity table
items.summary: In 1730, when soldiers arrived in Khejarli village in Rajasthan to fell trees for a royal palace, Amrita Devi Bishnoi wrapped her arms around a Khejri tree to protect it. She was killed, along with 362 others from the Bishnoi community, in an act of resistance that helped bring the tree-felling to a halt. More than two centuries later, in Uttarakhand, Gaura Devi and 27 women embraced trees in Reni village in 1974 to prevent the felling of about 1,000 trees. In Assam, the Hargila Army, founded in 2007 by conservationist Purnima Devi Barman, continues to mobilise rural women to protect the endangered greater adjutant stork and its nesting trees. From protecting sacred trees in Rajasthan to conserving forests in Uttarakhand and saving endangered birds in Assam, women across India have shaped the fight to protect biodiversity. Yet, their knowledge, leadership, and contributions do not always translate into an equal say in decisions about how nature is conserved, who controls natural resources, and where conservation funding goes. That gap is at the heart of gender negotiations at the 17th Conference of the Parties (COP17) to the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD), being held in Yerevan, Armenia. As countries review the implementation of the Gender Plan of Action (2023–2030), the negotiations raise a critical question: will the women who protect biodiversity on the ground have the power, resources, and recognition to shape the policies that govern it? Why gender negotiations at COP17 matter to India For India, the stakes extend beyond women's representation in conservation. Millions of people depend on forests, fisheries, and other natural resources for their livelihoods. This means that decisions about access, ownership, and management of biodiversity are particularly consequential for women in these communities. India has several legal and institutional mechanisms intended to bring women into biodiversity governance, but gaps in implementation continue to limit their influence over decisions affecting natural resources, a report by the CBD Women's Caucus has found. items.title: Andhra State Election Commission agrees to publish candidate affidavits online following PIL
items.summary: Follow TNM ’ s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. The Andhra Pradesh High Court on Friday, October 30, disposed of a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) after the State Election Commission (APSEC) confirmed it has issued orders to publish contesting candidates' nomination papers and affidavits online for upcoming local body elections. With the state set to vote on Sunday, November 1, the portal had not published affidavit details at the time of disposal of the PIL. The PIL in question was filed amid the ongoing violence in Andhra’s urban local body polls. The case was heard by a division bench comprising Chief Justice Lisa Gill and Justice Challa Gunaranjan. The government pleader representing APSEC informed Chief Justice Lisa Gill that the commission issued an official order the previous day directing that candidate affidavits and nomination details be uploaded and displayed on the APSEC portal. The petition was filed earlier in the week by Siva Karthik Valaparla, a resident of Nuzvid, Eluru district. The petitioner had approached the court seeking directions to compel the state election body to establish an online candidate disclosure system. On October 17, Siva Karthik submitted a formal representation via email and post to the State Election Commissioner. Drawing a parallel to the Election Commission of India’s (ECI) candidate affidavit portal, he had requested APSEC to create a dedicated web portal to publish nomination papers and affidavits organised by district, local body, ward, and candidate name to foster transparency and informed voting in local body polls. In its written response dated October 23, the APSEC initially rejected the request. The commission cited Section 36 of the Andhra Pradesh Municipal Corporations Act and the AP Municipalities (Conduct of Election of Members) Rules, stating that governing election laws only mandated physical submission of nomination papers directly to Returning Officers and contained no statutory requirement for online publication. Following the court's intervention, APSEC reversed its earlier stance and issued the necessary order to publish candidate affidavits on its portal, prompting the disposal. items.title: Madras HC issues notice on plea seeking probe into CJP leader Saurav Das’ ancestry
items.summary: The Madras High Court has issued notices to Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) spokesperson and journalist Saurav Das, along with several Union government departments, over a petition seeking an investigation into the journalist's ancestry, cancellation of his passport and Aadhaar, and the suspension of his social media accounts. The petition, filed by Ganesh Kumar Ramakumar, sought details of Saurav Das’ biological parents. It alleged that his real name is Yogesh Sharma and that he has Nepali origins. The petitioner has also sought an investigation into how the CJP leader obtained Indian identity documents despite his alleged Nepali ancestry. A bench of Chief Justice SA Dharmadhikari and Justice G Arul Murugan issued notices to the respondents, including the Regional Passport Officer in Chennai, the Chairperson of the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI), the Union Home Ministry, the Foreign Secretary in the Ministry of External Affairs, and Secretaries of the Ministries of Law and Justice and Electronics and Information Technology. Notices were also issued to the grievance officers of X (formerly Twitter) and Instagram. The court made the notices returnable in six weeks and adjourned the hearing, Live Law reported. Ganesh, a resident of Kanchipuram district, is the co-founder and director of software company Mahadhi Technologies. He has insisted that he is not pursuing the petition for “political gain, vendetta, media publicity, nor do I have any hidden agenda”. Instead, he claimed locus standi as a “concerned citizen of the state” interested in exposing “certain self-appointed critics of the government and the Judiciary” who allegedly misuse social media to spread “false and unsubstantiated frivolous allegations”. The petitioner alleged that Saurav Das, whose real name he claimed was “Yogesh Sharma”, was creating disharmony, anarchy, hatred, and unrest by repeatedly criticising and abusing the judiciary. As evidence, he attached a series of Saurav’s social media posts concerning the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and his criticism of the judiciary. Ganesh further claimed that Saurav was of Nepali origin and argued that the matter required investigation. “If found true, he cannot lecture about our government and our judiciary,” the petition stated.
